detail.description: The 38th Commonwealth Club World Affairs' Distinguished Citizens Awards Annual Gala 2026 will celebrate visionary leaders whose innovation, generosity and commitment to the public good are shaping a brighter future for our communities.
detail.title: Distinguished Citizens Awards Annual Gala 2026
detail.venue: The Fairmont Hotel, 950 Mason St., San Francisco, CA, 94108

detail.description: Frank Capra, the director of Mr. Smith Goes to Washington, It Happened One Night, and It’s a Wonderful Life, is renowned as one of the great chroniclers of the American heart—how we love, dream, hope and fight for our individuality. But Frank Capra was a far more complex artist than is usually reckoned and a far more complicated man than anyone knows. As Jimmy Stewart, his most famous collaborator, put it, “the best Frank Capra story is the story of his own life. It’s got more highs and lows than a roller coaster. It’s heartwarming.
detail.title: Sam Wasson: Frank Capra’s Own Wondrous Life
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California

detail.description: One of the most persistent and pernicious problems caused by patriarchal cultures is the internalization of inferiority in the socially powerless.
detail.title: Sheba Shobashini: How to Resist Adopting a Spiritual Inferiority Complex
detail.venue: The Commonwealth Club of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: What if we understood local media not simply as a source of news and information, but as essential civic infrastructure? At a moment when local journalism is shrinking, public trust is eroding, and communities are increasingly disconnected, we need to rethink the role media plays in the places we call home. A healthy civic life depends on more than informed residents. It depends on people feeling connected to one another, seeing themselves and their communities represented, having opportunities to participate in public life, and developing a shared sense of belonging and possibility.
detail.title: Media as Civic Infrastructure: Building the Culture and Communities We Need
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Toni Rembe Rock Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: Rob Mintz, chief curator at the Asian Art Museum and artist Nick Dong explore the intersections of art, technology and Buddhist awakening—a conversation with the artist and a museum curator. Integrating the invisible connections of sound, light and metal work to eliminate societal fractures and create a universal spiritual awareness, Oakland artist Nick Dong, a visionary craftsman, sculptor and engineer, brings to Commonwealth Club World Affairs a unique audiovisual experience that’s totally different from anything Club members have ever seen or heard before.
detail.title: The Intersection of Art Therapy and Spiritual Enlightenment: An Engineer’s Perspective!
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, 110 The Embarcadero, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: Today, California’s wine industry creates about $84 billion in economic activity in the state, supporting hundreds of thousands of jobs and contributing billions in state and federal taxes. Join us for an inside look at the deals, drama and drive behind one of America’s greatest wine dynasties when Michael Mondavi comes to the Club.
detail.title: Michael Mondavi Biography Book Launch—Deals Drama Drive: Michael Mondavi and the Making of Napa Valley
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: San Francisco has a rich journalism history that includes being home to the nation’s first investigative news organization, Mother Jones. The independent, nonprofit news outlet started in 1976 in an office above a McDonald’s restaurant, and has been exposing wrongdoing among governments and corporations, and holding the powerful to account for 50 years.
detail.title: 50 Years of Mother Jones, with Adam Hochschild and Monika Bauerlein
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Toni Rembe Rock Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: Are you a person who never tires of talking or thinking about philosophical, scientific or religious theories? Are you interested in psychological insights, or attempts at such insights, into human life? There are many who would insist that being realistic about human life means you should ignore such fundamental questions—starting around the time the ink dries on your diploma. But it is unrealistic to ignore the fundamental explanatory concepts that underlie each successful human civilization—concepts that sometimes help and sometimes hinder us in our pursuit of happiness.
detail.title: Imperfect Circles Discussion Group at the Orinda Library
detail.venue: Orinda Public Library, 26 Orinda Way, Orinda, CA, 94563

detail.description: The Second Life of Freddie Nole is a short documentary film that follows Freddie, a magnetic and deeply compassionate man, who spends his days meeting newly released citizens at the prison gates, offering not just a ride but a shot at redemption. Part buddy movie, part road trip film, the story unfolds over the course of a single day as Freddie and his friend Steve Chile, the first man he ever picked up, help Ed as he takes his first steps into freedom.
detail.title: ‘The Second Life of Freddie Nole’: Documentary Screening
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: In a world full of seemingly endless challenges, one human characteristic separates those who only see the world’s flaws from those who see its potential for change—and that characteristic is hope.
detail.title: Venture Philanthropy Leader Jim Bildner: Turning Hope Into Action
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Toni Rembe Rock Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: Fiercely independent journalist Amy Goodman has spent three decades holding the powerful to account, reporting from war zones and the Democracy Now! newsroom. Taking on politicians, CEOs and riot police, Goodman has reported some of the most urgent and underreported stories of our time.
detail.title: ‘Steal This Story, Please!’ Film Screening and Q&A with Amy Goodman and Tia Lessin
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: Appetizers prepared by United States Coast Guard culinary students. How many times a day do you ask the question, “What should I eat?” Are you confused and overwhelmed by the thousands of factory-made foods supermarkets sell? Or the abundance of diets (paleo, Mediterranean, low-fat, low-carb, low-calorie, intermittent fasting, vegan, vegetarian, carnivore) claimed to optimize your health and manage your weight?
detail.title: Fed Up: What Evolution Reveals about Food, Diet, Health and Eating Well
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Toni Rembe Rock Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: From the left, right and center, many Americans would agree that American government is broken. The country that built the national highway system and created Social Security and Medicare now seems to barely manage the basics. What went wrong?
detail.title: Nicholas Bagley: How Legal Reformers Accidentally Broke America
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: Have questions about weather and climate? Daniel Swain has answers. Swain’s research on “hydroclimate whiplash”—the extreme swings between floods and fires—is fundamental. But the general public knows him better as the host of the popular blog and YouTube channel “Weather West,” which has tens of thousands of subscribers. In his quest to make extreme weather, climate change, and associated natural hazards understandable and accurate in public discourse, Swain holds weekly “office hours” on YouTube and gives over 200 interviews a year across hundreds of media outlets.
detail.title: Daniel Swain: 2026 Stephen Schneider Award for Outstanding Climate Science Communication
detail.venue: The Commonwealth Club of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: A novelist and an economist walk into a bar. Outside, the world is in polycrisis. One of them spent 20 years in the belly of the beast, becoming the second youngest managing director in JPMorgan’s history, followed by a two-decade search after a close encounter with 9/11. The other has spent four decades writing novels set on Mars, in a flooded New York, and inside a ministry created to speak for generations not yet born. You might expect the banker to bring the hard facts and the novelist the imagination. On this evening, it may run the other way.
detail.title: The Novelist & the Economist: Kim Stanley Robinson and John Fullerton on the Story We Need Next
detail.venue: The Commonwealth Club of California, Toni Rembe Rock Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: In 2015, Europe faced its largest refugee crisis since World War II. Hundreds of thousands of people fled war, persecution and hardship, risking their lives in search of safety. For many, that journey meant crossing the dangerous waters between Turkey and Greece.
detail.title: Reading Californians: Jeanne Carstensen’s A Greek Tragedy—A Deadly Shipwreck During Europe’s 2015 Refugee Crisis
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California

detail.description: What if schools were not just places where students learn about the world, but places where they actively help shape the communities around them? Join us for this Transforming Our Region forum exploring how place-based education can connect students to their local environments, communities, and real-world challenges while contributing to broader systems change.
detail.title: Learning Through Place: How Schools Can Catalyze Community and Environmental Change
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Toni Rembe Rock Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: You are cordially invited to an evening of holiday cheer, good company, and great music at our annual Holiday Mixer. Co-presidents and Co-CEOs Gloria Duffy and Philip Yun will announce what exciting things await us in 2027 at Commonwealth Club World Affairs. Be in the know and learn about all the great programs the Club offers its members.
detail.title: Holiday Mixer at the Club 2026: Music, Art, Bites and Bevs
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: Join Vendela Vida, David Katznelson, and Ulf Olsson to celebrate their recent anthology of Swedish fiction, Out of the Darkness: Classic Short Fiction from Sweden, published by the University of Minnesota Press.
detail.title: Out of the Darkness: Rediscovering Classic Swedish Literature
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Toni Rembe Rock Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: We rely on encryption every day, usually without thinking about it. It protects our bank accounts, medical records, government systems, business communications, intellectual property, and much of the infrastructure that makes modern life work. But what happens if the mathematics behind some of those protections can be broken?
detail.title: The Quantum Threat: What Happens When Our Digital Locks Stop Working
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Toni Rembe Rock Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: What if the obsessive pursuit of health's itself making us sick? The global wellness economy is booming: biometric wearables, longevity podcasts, and biohacking influencers peddling supplements, cold plunges, and five-figure drug regimens. The pursuit of health and longevity has never been more complicated or more expensive.
detail.title: The Longevity Trap: Why the Obsessive Pursuit of Longevity Is Making Us Sick—and How to Actually Live Well
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, 110 The Embarcadero, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn has been in trouble almost from the moment Mark Twain published it, first in Britain in 1884 and then in the United States in 1885. The original objections included Huck’s bad behavior and socially subversive thinking, but also the book’s bad grammar and unconventional language.
detail.title: Should Huckleberry Finn Be Banned from Our Schools — For Its Own Good?
detail.venue: The Commonwealth Club of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: Masked troops of ICE and CBP are scooping up immigrants, occasionally shooting or beating one or two. Is this good policy? Immigration is a policy issue with both social and economic implications. Economics has something to say about both. This presentation will shed light on several aspects of immigration that tend to overwhelm the narrative. These are: crime, government support programs, and jobs. It will also raise other issues that ought to be contemplated when developing appropriate immigration policy. About the Speaker
detail.title: Jon Haveman: The Economics of Immigration
detail.venue: Lafayette Public Library, Don Tatzin Auditorium, Lafayette, CA, 94549

detail.description: Mary C. Daly is president and chief executive officer of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco. In that capacity, she serves the Twelfth Federal Reserve District in setting monetary policy. Prior to that, President Daly was the executive vice president and director of research at the San Francisco Fed, which she joined in 1996. Join us for a discussion on the economic implications of artificial intelligence and how it might impact productivity, employment and growth.
detail.title: AI and the Economy, with SF Fed’s Mary C. Daly
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: In The Left's War on Reality, Michael Shellenberger and Alex Gutentag, two former progressives, delve into the unsettling truth behind the left’s policies. What they uncover is far more troubling than mere unintended consequences. Through nine meticulously researched case studies, they reveal a shocking conclusion: the destruction caused by the left isn’t accidental—it’s deliberate.
detail.title: Michael Shellenberger and Alex Gutentag: The Left's War on Reality
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: David Y. Lei, born in Taiwan, immigrated to the United States in 1956. He began his career as a social worker in San Francisco’s Chinatown in the late 1960s, working with young people involved in Chinatown gangs. In 1981, he entered the business world, exporting consumer products to Mexico. He sold his business in 2003 and retired. Lei served as vice chair of the Asian Art Museum board and directed San Francisco’s Chinese New Year Parade from 1977 to 2006.
detail.title: Chinese Americans: The Most Litigious, Civilly Disobedient Americans
detail.venue: The Commonwealth Club of California, Toni Rembe Rock Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: Paulina Borsook’s work Cyberselfish—now in a current printing, has been rediscovered as "accidental prophecy"—has been called a sharp, prescient critique of Silicon Valley's emerging elite during the late-1990s dot-com boom. She identified several toxic cultural undercurrents that she says have now become mainstream realities across global tech infrastructure:
detail.title: From Cyberselfish to the Nerd Reich: The Rise of Radical Silicon Valley
detail.venue: Lafayette Public Library, Don Tatzin Auditorium, Lafayette, CA, 94549

detail.description: Former "MythBusters" co-host Adam Savage has been described as “a master maker,” “a nerd’s nerd,” and “somebody who blows stuff up.” In his 2020 book Every Tool’s a Hammer, he writes: “There was something special in the marriage between the structure of my brain and what I could do with my hands. When I made stuff, the world made sense to me. It felt like my superpower.” Savage first used that superpower in the special effects industry, working on films like Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace, Galaxy Quest, and the Matrix sequels.
detail.title: MythBusters’ Adam Savage on Finding Joy in Making Things
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: What distinguishes the prose of great novels? How have celebrated novelists shaped language into a lasting source of insight and aesthetic pleasure? The award-winning literary critic Robert Alter explores the literary devices and techniques novelists have used to write famous fiction.
detail.title: Robert Alter: The Language of Fiction, the Craft of Writing and the Pleasures of Reading
detail.venue: The Commonwealth Club of California, Toni Rembe Rock Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: Where You Find Me is a short film directed by Jen Tocquigny that follows Betty Ann Bruno's journey working as a Munchkin in The Wizard of Oz to finding her way back to her family’s roots. After her family moved away from Hollywood, her path was marked by many pivotal moments that shaped her career. Betty Ann took a job in the CIA, went through a period of civic activism in Oakland, then an eventual run for City Council. She went on to become a three-time Emmy Award-winning KTVU reporter—one of the first broadcast positions for Asian-American women.
detail.title: 'Where You Find Me' Film Screening and Q&A
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: How do scholars and experts rate the presidents? Who was smart, and who was not? Who was inept or corrupt?
detail.title: Little-Known (and Shocking) Revelations About the Character and Conduct of America’s Presidents
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, 110 The Embarcadero, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: Learn about the men and women who transformed America’s First Amendment from an unfulfilled promise into the world’s strongest protection for free speech.
detail.title: Nico Perrino: Free Speech Generation
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: What drove a few thousand men and women from the deserts and cities of western China to the front lines of Syria’s war? In her new book, Our Hearts Burned for Home, journalist Emily Feng unearths the untold story of Uyghur exiles who fled China’s expanding police state—only to become a pivotal force behind the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s regime. At the heart of this narrative is a startling paradox: Beijing’s repression, meant to crush dissent, instead scattered and radicalized a generation.
detail.title: NPR’s Emily Feng on How China’s Repression Fueled a Militant Movement…In Syria
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Toni Rembe Rock Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: The fossil fuel industry uses its immense profits to further its own interests—essentially, to slow the transition away from coal, oil, and gas—in many sectors, including the nation’s elite universities and top-tier climate science research programs.
detail.title: ProPublica, Stanford and UC Berkeley on the Influence of Fossil Fuel Funding in Academia
detail.venue: The Commonwealth Club of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: The Walter E. Hoadley Annual Economic Forecast, presented by Bank of America. The current state of the U.S. economy has been described as a “boomcession”: Even as a surge in AI investment is boosting the stock market and GDP, many ordinary Americans are feeling left behind. To be sure, the economy is still booming, at least on paper, and consumers are still spending, But inflation, rising gas prices, and borrowing costs are all putting the squeeze on households.
detail.title: The Economy 2027: Will the “Boomcession” Continue?
detail.venue: The Commonwealth Club of California, 110 The Embarcadero, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: In a visionary essay in Foreign Affairs, physicist Amory Lovins opened by asking, “Where are America's formal or de facto energy policies leading us? Where might we choose to go instead?” That was 50 years ago. And those critical questions remain just as relevant today, especially against the backdrop of geopolitical tensions, energy security concerns, and accelerating climate disruption.
detail.title: Amory Lovins on Disruptive Energy Futures
detail.venue: The Commonwealth Club of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: How can Silicon Valley produce better, human-centered, equitable technology?
detail.title: Timnit Gebru: The Rise of AI and the Radicalization of a Tech Idealist
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: Reading others’ personalities is something we all do every day. But how accurately? Some managers seem to be born with the ability to read, and then successfully manipulate, their sales staff. And some artists intuitively create images or songs that resonate deeply with how millions feel—even though they were hardly aware of those feelings themselves. But is reading others’ personalities accurately like that a skill that can be learned?
detail.title: George Hammond: Reading Others' Personalities
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: How are great brands built—and rebuilt? How do grand leaders ignite growth? The former president and CEO of Levi Strauss & Co. joins us for an exploration of how he accomplished those goals at the head of the iconic clothing company.
detail.title: Chip Bergh: A Levi’s Story
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: What does it take to move a room full of people? And what can the co-creator of Broadway's Freestyle Love Supreme teach us about how it happens? Join screenwriter-turned-organizational psychologist and author Lindsey Caplan and Anthony Veneziale, co-creator of the Tony Award-winning Freestyle Love Supreme alongside Lin-Manuel Miranda and Thomas Kail, for an evening that's part performance, part conversation, and anything but a traditional book talk.
detail.title: Lindsey Caplan and Anthony Veneziale: The Art and Science of What Moves Us and How to Move Others
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: In 1863, as the Civil War raged, Russian warships suddenly appeared in New York and San Francisco, sparking celebrations across the North and raising hopes that Russia might support the United States should Britain and France recognize the Confederacy.
detail.title: Vladimir Alexandrov: Imperial Russian Support for the Union During the Civil War
detail.venue: The Commonwealth Club of California, Toni Rembe Rock Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: In the midterm election, Americans told pollsters their top priorities included affordability and corruption. The result was a nationwide wave of flipped seats and legislative takeovers.
detail.title: Zephyr Teachout: Anti-Monopoly, A Citizen’s Guide
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Toni Rembe Rock Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: The man who wrote The Karate Kid, The Fifth Element, and the Taken franchises was also an international drug trafficker. True, and he says that’s not even the craziest part of his life, which he recounts in his new memoir A Very Particular Set of Skills. Come see him at Commonwealth Club World Affairs to hear all about it.
detail.title: Robert Mark Kamen: A Screenwriter’s Journey
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: Ludwig van Beethoven died on March 26, 1827, after a lifetime of composing music that still thrills audiences around the world. Humanities West celebrates those invaluable cultural contributions on the 200th Anniversary of his death by featuring two Bay Area music scholars and popular lecturers—and a special focus on the Ode to Joy of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony. The Road to the Ninth: Beethoven’s Symphonic Journey
detail.title: Humanities West Presents Beethoven the Revolutionary
detail.venue: The Commonwealth Club of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: Sit down with Humanities West to enjoy one of the first stand-up comedians: Mark Twain. In his own words. Mark Twain’s worldwide on-stage performances in the 19th century were successfully imitated by many great actors throughout the second half of the 20th century, including Mark Dawidziak, who has been impersonating Twain for over 45 years. And no longer needs any makeup to pull that off.
detail.title: Humanities West presents Mark Twain in His Own Words
detail.venue: The Commonwealth Club of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105

detail.description: What if the measure of a significant life isn't what you accumulated, but what you awakened in other people? "An Evening with Dan Ashley" is not simply an interview with a celebrated broadcaster and musician. It is a 65-minute journey through the "side quests" that shaped Dan's life—and the people who became better, braver and more purposeful because he chose to pursue them. This evening asks a simple question: Who will you become because of the life you've been given?
detail.title: An Evening with Dan Ashley: Side Quests to Significance
detail.venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, Taube Family Auditorium, San Francisco, CA, 94105
